item.title: CKB Talk Daily Brief - 2026-11-07
item.description: ## 今日发生了什么 从论坛发帖看，今天的主线是 CKB 生态项目更新与 Spark Program 付款、评审同步推进，并非单一话题。[S03, S15, S20, S23] 同时，官网 PR 讨论出现明显分歧：一方认为不更新官网有原因，另一方认为全球官网和海外社媒长期不维护会损害开发者和资金进入。[S08, S09] 此外，Cellula on Fiber 披露了故障场景测试结果并报告 Fiber bug，CKBuilders 成员也发布或介绍了两个新项目。[S21, S01, S02] ## 重点话题 官网 PR 争论升温：silenceport 称“不更新官网是有原因的”，并称不要帮倒忙 [S08]；Thinker 反驳把停更说成防监管是偷换概念，强调全球官网和海外社媒是面向全球开发者的基础服务 [S09]；psawyerberlin 提出缩小范围、只做时间中性的内容移除清理 [S10]。 QuotaCell 更新：作者称已从测试代币推进到可用的 CKB spending Pocket [S03]；回应者认可关闭成本降到 134 CKB 是明显改进 [S04]；随后讨论 keeper 钱包独立且保持小额可限制密钥泄露损害，但需要手动充值 [S04, S05]。 Cellula on Fiber 故障测试：团队称跑了支付中途切断、崩溃、重试三个场景且都通过，最终只支付一次、重试被拒绝 [S21]；还发现并报告 Fiber 小 bug（#1724）[S21]；ArthurZhang 表达赞赏 [S22]。 Spark Program 拨款与沟通流程：MeterNet...

item.title: Message in a Cell: seal a letter, a photo or a video with CKB until a day that matters (1 posts)
item.description: Hi everyone! I’m Linnette from the CKBuilders program. After CadencePay ( CadencePay: recurring payments on CKB where the person paying stays in control ), here’s the other project I built: Message in a Cell. The moment it felt real A friend tried it and sealed a message for me. When the countdown ended I opened it, and the letter and the CKB were mine. It was a small thing, but it felt like getting a real letter, from a blockchain. What it does You write a letter, add a photo or record a video or voice note, put some CKB in with it, and seal it until a date. item.title: CadencePay: recurring payments on CKB where the person paying stays in control (1 posts)
item.description: Hi everyone! I’m Linnette, a builder in the CKBuilders program, based in Nairobi. I’d love to introduce the project I built as my capstone. The problem Every subscription I’ve had could take more than I agreed to, or keep charging after I left. Creators here in Kenya deserve steady income without a platform taking a cut or sitting on their money. I wanted paying someone over time to feel like handing over cash, not handing over your wallet. What CadencePay does A member funds their own subscription cell, and one type script enforces the deal: the creator can collect exactly the agreed amount, at most once per period, always paid to them; the price, period and recipient can never change;...

item.title: QuotaCell: Let your team spend without handing over the treasury (3 posts)
item.description: QuotaCell update: From test tokens to a working CKB spending Pocket When I first shared QuotaCell, I was trying to solve a simple problem. How do you let contributors, teammates or automated agents pay project expenses without giving them the main treasury key or approving every payment yourself? The first experiments showed that CKB could enforce spending limits directly on-chain. But they were still using synthetic test tokens and a preconfigured setup. The feedback from @Ayoub_Lesfer and @ArthurZhang raised important questions about payments happening simultaneously, uncertain transaction outcomes, and the 600 CKB that remained locked after closing a Pocket. item.title: Spark Program | CellFlow — Durable CCC Transaction Recovery PoC (1 posts)
item.description: Thank you for reviewing the CellFlow proposal and providing clear, constructive feedback. I understand the committee’s concerns regarding the lack of demonstrated ecosystem demand and the additional operational complexity introduced by the proposed architecture. I agree that any recovery solution should complement CCC and CKB RPC rather than duplicate their existing capabilities or impose unnecessary infrastructure requirements. Moving forward, I will focus on validating the problem through concrete developer use cases and exploring a more lightweight, optional approach that better aligns with the current CKB ecosystem. item.description: This is exactly the same issue I raised earlier about managing the @NervosNetwork account on X. item.title: Spark Program | NNCBN - Nervos Network Community Boot Nodes (4 posts)
item.description: Great to see this moving. A community bootnode on the Brazil–Portugal cable, home-hosted and on Qubes OS, adds exactly the kind of diversity the network lacks. I’d like to suggest a connection with a project I’m building, the CKB Service Runner (CSR). It’s a small side application that runs beside a fully synced full node. I think both projects could benefit. What CSR could give NNCBN Independent, verifiable uptime evidence. The curated bootnode list needs ongoing proof that nodes stay reachable and synced. item.title: Noir-CKB: the private tally is live on CKB testnet, try it yourself (1 posts)
item.description: GM xiaomao, congrats on getting this live, and on running a real ceremony instead of asking us to trust one key. Rebuilding the public inputs from the transaction itself is a neat answer to replay. On your question 2: I’ve been thinking about on-chain voting on CKB, where encrypted tallies have to stay hidden until disclosure. A proof bound to one ballot cell and one tally transition is the kind of thing that design space needs. Two loose thoughts, in case they’re useful: Fee payer: you list it as a remaining leak. item.title: Spark Program | Bees Network — Decentralized Observation Layer for AI Agents on CKB (1 posts)
item.description: Hi @NOrththebear, Sorry to see this one rejected. The MVP and the cell-based accounting are solid work. Reading the committee’s reason (bootstrapping node supply, ongoing incentives, demand), I think there’s a natural overlap with something I’m building, and maybe a way to share the hard part instead of each of us solving it alone. I’m working on CKB Service Runner (CSR), a side application that runs next to a fully synced CKB node and lets operators run jobs for tips. A public Network Monitor ranks runners by availability, age and network diversity (ASN, region, country). item.title: [DIS] Cellula on Fiber: a wallet, a checkout and an AI agent on a public mainnet LSP (2 posts)
item.description: Thanks Arthur, good list. We ran all three, and all three passed. Payment cut off halfway, a crash, then a retry. The person paid once, the shop was paid once, and the retry was refused. We also found a small bug in Fiber and reported it: nervosnetwork/fiber#1724. Connection lost until the channel is closed. Every payment ended correctly, and the payer ended with exactly the right balance. Leaving with the LSP switched off. With only the recovery file, the wallet got all its money back. We also did the same exit from the wallet’s own recovery page, on the public testnet: all the money came back within three hours. One small payment was still in progress when the LSP went down.
